content.text: No non-compete binding PB exists; the only exclusivity covenant runs against SFJ.

input.quote: 3.19 Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ. During the applicable Exclusive Period, SFJ shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, either by itself or through a Third Party, conduct human clinical trials of, or sell, offer for sale or have sold:
input.rationale: The only exclusivity/competing-product covenant in the Agreement (Section 3.19, read with the "Exclusive Period", "Competing Product" and "Brilinta Competing Product" definitions) binds SFJ and its Affiliates, i.e. the counterparty, and therefore operates in our favour. A full-text review found no covenant restricting PB from developing, manufacturing, marketing or selling any product, and no field-of-use or territory restriction on PB; the restrictions on PB in Article 7 (Sections 7.5.1–7.5.7) are financing/negative-pledge and licensing-consent covenants rather than non-competes, and Section 15 reserves to PB all rights not expressly granted. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is proposed. We note only that the consent requirement for non-Excluded Licensing Transactions in Section 7.5.5 constrains how PB may out-license the Product; that is a separate financing-covenant issue and is addressed under the negative-covenant rules, not double-flagged here.
